newsitem.title: UK: COSCO to set up separate tanker operating company.
newsitem.headline: COSCO to set up separate tanker operating company.

text.p: Chinese state shipping group COSCO is to set up a new company to manage and operate the group's tanker and LPG fleet, a China expert with a maritime legal company said Friday.

Sinclair, Roche & Temperley lawyer Nicholas Woo, who were legal consultants at Singapore joint venture COSCO-KSH until March 1996, said China's largest shipping group would set up two new companies in the immediate future.
"One will manage and operate the remainder of COSCO's general and specialised fleet and another will manage and operate COSCO's tanker and LPG fleet," he said.
The new tanker company will probably be based in Dalian, Woo said in a speech at the Baltic Exchange.
COSCO currently operates 22 tankers ranging in size from 12,650 dwt to 67,957 dwt, according to London-based Gibson Shipbrokers.
The moves would complete COSCO's restructuring which has been in process since 1993, Woo added.
The group has already set up ship managing and operating companies for its container and bulk fleets, based in Beijing.
Container ship operator COSCON manages a fleet of abour 150 vessels and has entered joint ventures with international operators such as K Line of Japan and Taiwanese firm Yang Ming Marine Transport.
"They are continually on the lookout for other operators who may be able to provide mutually beneficial alliances," he said.
Bulk operator COSBULK has a fleet of about 115 vessels representing about 6 million dwt. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
